gallery.filename: Adderley Street, Cape Town, looking NE - ca. 1897.jpg
gallery.title: File:Adderley Street, Cape Town, looking NE - ca. 1897.jpg
gallery.description: Original caption reads: "View of Adderley Street, Cape Town from Longmarket Street. This thoroughfare, which one might term "the leading street of South Africa", is thronged during the greater part of the day by a busy crowd of shoppers and pedestrians. The shops are for the most part situated on the north side of the street , and are decked with all the latest novelties from Europe. Electric trams start from the centre of Adderley Street for all parts of the town and suburbs, and are considered the finest and most complete "South of the line"."

gallery.title: File:Police at Houses of Parliament.jpg
gallery.description: 2014 Israel–Gaza conflict: On Saturday 9 August 2014, the National Coalition for Palestine called a pro-Palestine march in Cape Town. On the following day, the South African Zionist Federation held a Solidarity Rally for Israel in Hatfield Street in Cape Town, and pro-Palestine protesters came out again to show their support for Palestine. These police vehicles outside the Houses of Parliament were blocking vehicle access to Hatfield Street. (News article)

gallery.title: File:Port of Cape Town.jpg
gallery.description: The port of Cape Town remains open 24 hours a day 7 days a week. The entrance channel's depth below chart datum is -15.9m, -15.4m at the 180m wide entrance into Duncan Dock and -14m at the entrance to Ben Schoeman Dock. The depth in the Duncan Dock varies between -9.9m near the repair quay to -12.4m at the tanker basin. Ben Schoeman Dock varies from -9m to -13.9m. Dredging is currently (i.e. 2010) underway in the Ben Schoeman Dock (container terminal) to provide deeper berths for new generation container shipping.
